lines: Tellement que s'il a ſongé ceſte nou-
uelle impudẽce, & impoſture, ne s'en faut
Bien que la loy preſume des hommes, que chacun eſt
bon, bien viuant, & d'honneſte conuerſation {a}, & que
nul d'eux ha intention de mal faire {b}: toutesfois en ce-
luy qui vne fois a eſté mauuais & ſurprins en quelque
meſchanceté, la loy à grande raiſon penſe & le preſume
eſtre touſiours tel, en la meſme eſpece de mauuaiſtié {c}.
comme par exemple vn qui aura quelquefois deſrobé,
ſ'il eſt derechef accuſé de larrecin, pour ſi petite preuue
d'autre coniecture qu'il y aye, facilement ou le preſu-
mera pour le iourd'huy eſtre laron. Et elle qui aura vne
fois paillardé, qu'elle mal-verſe encores: & cil qu'il
en la premiere accuſatiõ aura eſté calomniateur, l'eſtré
encor en la ſeconde {d}. Deſquels & ſemblables, la raiſõ
n'eſt pas mal-aiſée à entendre: car il eſt vray-ſemblable
qu'en la volonté de fait, ou de parole declarée, chacun
d'accident, ou qualité (qui conſiſte en fait) facilement
ne ſe preſume point {f}. Ains pluſtoſt on tire argument
& coniecture du paſſé, au temps preſent & a l'aduenir {g}:
comme celuy qu'on a cognu vne fois riche, on le pre-
ſume encor pour le iourd'huy riche, ou pauure; encor
pauure. vn qui a eſté ſeigueur d'vn lieu, l'eſtré par apres:
vn ſuiet, l'eſtre encores. & ainſi des ſemblables {h}.
Au contraire, que le priſonnier fuſt veri-
tablement Martin Guerre, y auoit trente
eſtoyent les quatre ſeurs dudit Martin,

uncertain.note: marker k (the alphabet run carried over from p057) has no keyed note on this page. Its only candidate is the unkeyed two-line note 'Panor' au c. ij.' / 'de maled.' (margin_notes[0]), printed with no key letter beside the TEXTE paragraph two lines below the marker; it is almost certainly the citation for {k}, but nothing keys it, so it is recorded with key null and the pairing is stated here rather than imposed.

no key letter is printed before this note (margin-1.jpg, 4x): the line begins directly with the italic capital P at the note column's left edge. Recorded with key null per §4; see blocks[0].lines[0] for its probable pairing with marker {k}. The print sets 'Panor'au' tight after the raised apostrophe-shaped abbreviation stroke; 'Panor'' (Panormitanus) and 'au' are distinct words, so a space is set between them per §1 word division. 'ij' is the italic ÿ-shaped ij sort, transcribed decomposed.

sic, wrong sort: the second letter of the heading is a capital B (two closed bowls, rounded right side, clear at 4x on body-1.jpg), not the E of the page's second TEXTE heading or of ARREST. Transcribed as printed. Reader A read it as E.

uncertain.text: uelle impudẽce, & impoſture, ne s'en faut
uncertain.note: the mark over the first e of 'impudẽce' is a flat, slightly wavy horizontal bar with hooked ends (4x, body-2.jpg), unlike the steep short wedge of the acutes at 'ſongé' and 'volonté'; read as the nasal tilde (= impudence). 's'il', 's'en' and 'esbahir' in this large type have a round s, as printed.

uncertain.text: fois paillardé, qu'elle mal-verſe encores: & cil qu'il
uncertain.note: 'cil' is set with a hairline gap after the c; transcribed as one word per §1. 'mal-verſe' carries a true mid-line hyphen; the mark after 'encores' is a colon.

uncertain.text: en la premiere accuſatiõ aura eſté calomniateur, l'eſtré
uncertain.note: sic: 'l'eſtré' carries a clear acute on the final e (also at blocks[4].lines[21]); blocks[4].lines[22] has plain 'l'eſtre'. Transcribed as printed in all three places.

uncertain.text: comme celuy qu'on a cognu vne fois riche, on le pre-
uncertain.note: the line-end word-break sign after 'pre' is a small round point raised to mid x-height, not the level bar used at 'ce-' and 'veri-'; the same raised point ends 'preſu-' (lines[8]). Both transcribed as '-' per §1.

uncertain.text: ſume encor pour le iourd'huy riche, ou pauure; encor
uncertain.note: the mark after 'pauure' is read as a semicolon (body-6.jpg, first line, 4x): the upper element is a round dot, the lower a narrow vertical wedge reaching below the baseline, unlike the two even round dots of the page's colons ('entendre: car', 'encores:') though its tail is much shorter than the comma after 'riche'. A colon is the alternative reading. Both readers read a semicolon.

uncertain.text: pauure. vn qui a eſté ſeigueur d'vn lieu, l'eſtré par apres:
uncertain.note: sic, wrong sort: 'ſeigueur' for seigneur — at 4x the letter after g is an unambiguous u (two stems joined by a bottom bow). Transcribed as printed. A faint stray ink arc crossing this line and the one above between 'lieu' and 'apres' is not type.
a round baseline period follows 'teſmoins' although lower-case 'entre' follows; transcribed as printed (the page uses mid-sentence periods freely: 'laron. Et', 'pauure. vn', 'encores. & ainſi').

the line opens with an italic capital P (no stroke through stem or descender, so not ꝑ/ꝓ) followed by a space and 'rogo.'; the citation wants the paragraph sign (§ rogo), so the P is probably the printer's substitute for §. Transcribed as printed; the same sort appears in 'l. ſi cui. P.' (note d) and 'l. ſicut P. ſu' (note g).

the p of 'p̃te' carries a short horizontal abbreviation bar across the top of its stem, projecting to the left (margin-2.jpg, 6x), absent from the other italic p's on the page ('paruu' directly below, 'ſump.', 'pro', 'proba'). Transcribed as p + combining tilde per §2; the reference runs on to 'ſump.' (de præſump.). Reader B gave a plain p.
the mark closing the line is a comma (short tail below the baseline); 'nõ' has a straight bar over the o.

a solid baseline period is printed directly after the ampersand, set tight ('&.'), the same size as the period after 'cond' (margin-2.jpg, 4x). The validator enforces the §1 rule that '&' takes a space on both sides and rejects '&.', so the line is recorded as '& .'; the print has '&.' with no space.

a small faint dot stands on the baseline directly after the initial l, in the position of the period the other notes print after 'l.' (margin-2.jpg, note g, 7x); it is much lighter and smaller than those periods, so it is read as a lightly inked period sort rather than a speck. Reader B transcribed no point. A human may wish to confirm on the full-resolution scan.

sic: the line ends 'poſti' and runs on to 'dens' — 'poſtidens' where the citation wants 'poſſidens'. At 4x (margin-3.jpg) the second tall letter has a clear crossbar and curled top (italic t), not a long ſ; compare the 'poſ-' / 'ſideris' break in note h. Wrong sort, transcribed as printed.

beside_line values follow reader A, who measured row centres on pages/read/p058.jpg: the margin is set solid in a smaller face with tighter leading than the body, so notes drift relative to their markers (note g begins several body lines above its {g}). Each beside_line is the body line nearest the note's first line, accurate to about half a line.

page furniture: folio '58' top left, running head ARREST DV in spaced capitals closed up, the three headings in spaced capitals, no signature, catchword, ornament or foot citation block (foot.jpg and body-8.jpg are blank). A brown damp stain across the top-left corner does not touch the type. Spacing normalized throughout per §1 (words set tight, spaces before punctuation, space inside the closing parenthesis of '(qui conſiſte en fait )').

decisions.reason: body-1.jpg heading at 4x: the second sort has two closed bowls and a rounded right side, a capital B; the E's of ARREST and of the lower TEXTE are plain three-armed E's. Wrong sort, transcribed as printed with a sic note.

margin-1.jpg at 4x: the raised mark after 'Panor' is an abbreviation stroke closing the word Panor(mitanus); 'au' is a distinct word, so the §1 word-division rule sets one space between them even though the compositor set them tight.

margin-2.jpg at 6x: the p carries a flat bar across the top of its stem projecting left, which no other italic p on the page has (compare 'paruu' directly below); an abbreviation stroke, transcribed as p + combining tilde per §2.

margin-2.jpg note g at 7x: a small faint dot sits on the baseline directly after the l, exactly where the other notes print the period of 'l.'; read as a lightly inked period. Faint, so noted in uncertain.

both readers carried the normalizer's '& .'; the print sets a solid period tight against the ampersand ('&.', margin-2.jpg, 4x). The validator rejects '&.' (§1 spacing), so '& .' is kept with an uncertain note recording the print's form.
